lessons.title: しょうちする (shōchi suru) — to consent; to agree to a request
lessons.gloss: to consent; to agree to a request

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for rather, then the Japanese for to nod.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: しょうちする

segments.text: しょうちする — shōchi suru — "to consent; to agree to a request".
あにが たのんだので、しょうちしました。 — ani ga tanonda node, shōchi shimashita — "My brother asked me, so I agreed."
Polite しょうちします, shōchishimasu; a する verb. Past (polite): てんいんが しょうちしました。, ten'in ga shōchi shimashita.

しょうちする (shōchi suru) is built from a Sino-Japanese noun and the native verb suru, "to do". The noun, shōchi, is two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese: shō, "acquiesce" (Middle Chinese dzying) and chi, "know" (trje) (KANJIDIC2; JMdict; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

segments.instruction: shōchi suru
shōchi suru, once more
ani ga tanonda node, shōchi shimashita — My brother asked me, so I agreed.
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *ani ga tanonda node, shōchi shimashita* — My brother asked me, so I agreed.]

segments.instruction: say the Japanese for rather, then the Japanese for to nod, then say shōchi suru again
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say the Japanese for rather, then the Japanese for to nod, then say *shōchi suru* again]

segments.text: What does しょうちする (shōchi suru) mean? ("To consent; to agree to a request".) Say it once more.

feedback.correct: Right: しょうちする (shōchi suru) is 'to consent; to agree to a request'.
feedback.incorrect: 'To consent' is しょうちする (shōchi suru).

lessons.title: うけいれる (ukeireru) — to accept; to take in

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for to nod, then the Japanese for to consent.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: うけいれる

segments.text: うけいれる — ukeireru — "to accept; to take in".
みんなが さんせいしたので、かいしゃは ていあんを うけいれました。 — minna ga sansei shita node, kaisha wa teian o ukeiremashita — "Everyone agreed, so the company accepted the proposal."
Polite うけいれます, ukeiremasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): かいしゃが うけいれました。, kaisha ga ukeiremashita.

うけいれる (ukeireru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese: it is built from ukeru, "to receive" and ireru, "to put in", and its kanji were attached later as kun'yomi (JMdict).
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: もちろん

segments.text: もちろん — mochiron — "of course".
じかんが あるから、もちろん てつだいます。 — jikan ga aru kara, mochiron tetsudaimasu — "I have time, so of course I will help."

もちろん (mochiron) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are mochi, "not" and ron, "argument" (Middle Chinese lwon) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription). JMdict notes that it is usually written in kana.
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: ぜひ

segments.text: ぜひ — zehi — "by all means; without fail".
おもしろいので、ぜひ よんで ください。 — omoshiroi node, zehi yonde kudasai — "It is interesting, so do read it."

ぜひ (zehi) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are ze, "right" (Middle Chinese dzyeX) and hi, "negative" (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).

lessons.title: もうしでる (mōshideru) — to come forward; to offer

blocks.title: You'll want to know: もうしでる

segments.text: もうしでる — mōshideru — "to come forward; to offer".
あには じかんが あったので、もうしでました。 — ani wa jikan ga atta node, mōshidemashita — "My brother had time, so he offered to help."
Polite もうしでます, mōshidemasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): あにが もうしでました。, ani ga mōshidemashita.

もうしでる (mōshideru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese: it is built from mōsu, "to say (humble)" and deru, "to come out", and its kanji were attached later as kun'yomi (JMdict).
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

segments.text: To agree? (さんせいする, sansei suru.) To be against? (はんたいする, hantai suru.) A discussion? (ぎろん, giron.) To propose? (ていあんする, teian suru.) A conclusion? (けつろん, ketsuron.) To explain? (せつめいする, setsumei suru.) To be convinced? (なっとくする, nattoku suru.) Grounds for a claim? (こんきょ, konkyo.) A meaning? (いみ, imi.) For what reason? (なぜ, naze.) One's real feelings? (ほんね, honne.) The official line? (たてまえ, tatemae.) To admit? (みとめる, mitomeru.) To misunderstand? (ごかいする, gokai suru.) In earnest? (ほんき, honki.) A point of view? (たちば, tachiba.) A doubt? (ぎもん, gimon.) To insist? (しゅちょうする, shuchō suru.) To comprehend? (りかいする, rikai suru.) Especially? (とくに, tokuni.) Absolutely? (ぜったい, zettai.) Without fail? (かならず, kanarazu.) As expected? (やはり, yahari.) Rather? (むしろ, mushiro.) To nod? (うなずく, unazuku.) To consent? (しょうちする, shōchi suru.) To take in? (うけいれる, ukeireru.) Of course? (もちろん, mochiron.) By all means? (ぜひ, zehi.) To come forward? (もうしでる, mōshideru.)

feedback.correct: Right: さんせいする (sansei suru) is 'to agree; to be in favour'.
feedback.incorrect: 'To agree' is さんせいする (sansei suru).
